text.p: The London Metal Exchange's copper contract experienced another day of widespread, erratic price movements as traders remained nervous and uncertain about the market's near-term direction.
Other metals trundled along in copper's wake but with much more restricted price movements.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index was 0.40 points lower at 241.62.

"Copper is stuck in a $50 range, but the option declaration is keeping the market on edge," said Martin Squires, analyst at brokers Rudolf Wolff and Co, referring to Wednesday's LME December options declaration which was one of the major factors behind recent volatility. The three months delivery price twice swept down towards support at $2,150 before bouncing - the first time reflecting a smaller than expected LME stocks rise of 1,000 tonnes and the second on a nerve-twitching widening in the cash/threes backwardation. Cash/threes ended at $170 against $150 at one stage and three months last traded at $2,183, down $4 from Monday.

Aluminium proved the most resilient, managing to hold steady after a modest LME stocks fall before some late shortcovering took it to a $9 gain with last three months delivery business at $1,527 a tonne.
Lead absorbed some liquidation on a dip to $681 in the early afternoon but then rallied with lost production at Doe Run still a background factor. Last business was at $686, down $2.
Zinc was shaky but found some support around $1,060 before ending at $1,061, down $5 a tonne.
Nickel absorbed the impact of a 654 tonnes LME stocks rise and held steady for most of the day to end at $6,835, down $5.
Tin moved narrowly and last traded at $6,080, down $20, and alloy ended at $1,368, up $2 a tonne.

CBOT wheat futures were lower at midsession on the posting Tuesday of 700,000 bushels of wheat notices for delivery on the December contract, traders said. "December wheat is under pressure on deliveries and the Australian wheat crop," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics Tuesday said the 1996-97 Australian wheat crop would total 21.3 million tonnes, above the previous forecast of 20.9 million. At 1112 CST, wheat was 1/2 to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 7-1/4 at $3.86 a bushel.

Technically-driven fund selling and a dearth of buying interest pressured CSCE world sugar futures to settle sharply weaker and barely above the day's lows, market sources said. March closed the session down 0.39 to 10.27, traded 10.65 to 10.23. The back months settled 0.32 to 0.25 lower.

NYMEX crude fell Tuesday morning after three crude ports in Mexico were reopened after being shut Monday due to bad weather, traders said. "The opening of the ports is what started the decline in crude," said Al Lindseth, a trader with GSC Energy. At 1111 EST, January crude was off 14 cents a barrel at $24.66. January heating oil retraced a loss of almost 1.50 cents to stand at 73.50 cents, off 0.07 cent a gallon.
